headline: Sensex and Nifty end Muhurat Trading session in red, snapping seven-day rally on Diwali

marketStatus.message: Today is Diwali Laxmi Pujan. NSE will conduct Muhurat Trading. Exact trading timings are notified separately by NSE.

why: Indices edged lower post the closing auction session, ending in the red on Diwali for the first time in several years.
The minor dip in Sensex and Nifty broke an eight-day/seven-day winning streak on Dalal Street.
Losses in major heavyweight stocks such as Bharti Airtel and Infosys weighed on the indices during the session.
Investors balanced early festive buying enthusiasm against global macro cues and inflation data outlook.
whatHappening: NSE and BSE conducted the traditional Muhurat Trading session to mark Diwali Laxmi Pujan and Samvat 2083.
Indices initially rallied during the session, with the Sensex jumping up to 400 points and Nifty crossing 25,100.
Nifty surrendered its initial gains to close below the 25,000 mark after the closing auction session.
NSE Chief Ashish Kumar Chauhan advised investors to avoid F&O trading, ignore stock tips, and maintain a long-term approach.
summary: Indian stock markets concluded the special Diwali Muhurat Trading session in the red, breaking a 7-day winning streak. Although indices surged early in the session with Sensex rising nearly 400 points, gains pulled back during the closing auction with Nifty falling below 25,000. Heavyweights Bharti Airtel and Infosys featured among the top losers during the short session.
